intent.raw_query: Portugal Algarve, $2200, beach holiday with wine tasting, September 2026 from London

experiences.name: Meia Praia Beach Day
experiences.description: Spend a relaxing day at Meia Praia, one of the longest and most accessible beaches in the Algarve, located just minutes from Lagos town center. Ideal for arriving travelers on Day 1 since it is walkable from central Lagos hotels, allowing you to unwind after a late evening flight without needing transport. Rent a sun lounger, swim in calm Atlantic waters, and enjoy beachside snacks from nearby kiosks.

experiences.name: Algarve Wine Tasting at Quinta dos Vales
experiences.description: Visit Quinta dos Vales, a renowned winery in Estômbar, just 15 minutes from Lagoa and easily accessible from central Algarve hotels. Enjoy a guided tour of the vineyards and wine cellar followed by a tasting of regional Algarve wines including Negra Mole and Syrah varieties. Booking a morning session ensures you make the most of the day without wasting afternoon beach time. Staying in Lagoa or Carvoeiro puts you within easy reach of this hub.

experiences.name: Praia da Marinha Coastal Walk and Swim
experiences.description: Explore the dramatic golden limestone cliffs and crystal-clear coves of Praia da Marinha, consistently rated one of Europe's most beautiful beaches. The coastal walking trail connecting Marinha to Benagil takes roughly 90 minutes and rewards hikers with stunning sea views and hidden grottos. Staying in Carvoeiro or Lagoa places you within a 10-minute drive, making this a seamless half-day activity without long transfers.

experiences.name: Benagil Sea Cave Kayak Tour
experiences.description: Paddle into the iconic Benagil Cave, one of the Algarve's most photographed natural wonders, on a guided kayak tour departing directly from Benagil Beach. Morning departures offer calmer seas and softer light for photography. Tours last approximately 2 hours and cover nearby sea arches and hidden beaches. Choosing accommodation in Carvoeiro or Lagoa keeps you within a short drive of the departure point, eliminating the need for long cross-region transfers.

experiences.name: Silves Wine and Culture Evening Tour
experiences.description: Join a small-group evening tour of Silves, the historic Moorish capital of the Algarve, combining a visit to the impressive red sandstone castle with a curated tasting of local wines at a traditional adega in the old town. Evening tours avoid midday heat and make excellent use of late-afternoon hours after a beach morning. Silves is centrally located and reachable within 20 minutes from Lagoa or Carvoeiro hotels, making it a practical and enriching end to a full day.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Portugal Algarve
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Faro Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Collect luggage and arrange transfer to Lagoa Boutique Stay (approx. 45 min by bus or shared shuttle, budget ~€5-8 by Eva Bus).
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to Lagoa Boutique Stay, freshen up, and take a leisurely stroll around Lagoa town centre. Explore the charming Igreja Matriz de Lagoa (free entry) and the local market square to get oriented.
day_by_day.evening: Easy first evening — walk along the main pedestrian street in Lagoa, grab a casual dinner at a local tasca, and enjoy a glass of Algarve wine to unwind after travel.

meals.breakfast: Grab a snack or coffee at the airport upon arrival
meals.lunch: Skip or grab a pastel de nata and coffee at a café near Lagoa centre (~€2-3)
meals.dinner: Tasca O Zé in Lagoa town — hearty Portuguese pork or fish dish with house wine (~€10-12 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Eva Bus line from Faro Airport to Lagoa is the most budget-friendly transfer option. Buy a return ticket to save money. September weather in Algarve is warm and sunny, typically 25-28°C — perfect beach weather.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Praia de Carvoeiro, one of the most picturesque beaches near Lagoa (10 min by bus or taxi). Arrive early to claim a spot on the golden sand, swim in the clear Atlantic waters, and explore the dramatic cliff formations.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk the Algar Seco coastal boardwalk (free) — a stunning natural rock formation with sea caves and arches just a 20-minute walk east of Carvoeiro beach. Bring water and sunscreen.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagoa and visit a local adega (wine cellar). Lagoa is famous for its DO Lagoa wines — ask the hotel for a recommendation for a free or low-cost tasting at a cooperative like Adega do Cantor area cooperatives.

meals.breakfast: Café near hotel — coffee and toast with butter and jam (torrada) ~€2.50
meals.lunch: Beach snack bar at Carvoeiro — grilled sardine sandwich and a beer (~€7-9)
meals.dinner: Mercado de Lagoa area — pick up fresh produce and local cheese for a self-catered picnic dinner (~€5-7)

day_by_day.notes: Praia de Carvoeiro is reachable by local bus from Lagoa for about €1.50 each way. The Algar Seco walk is completely free and one of the most scenic spots in the Algarve.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Silves — take the train from Lagoa-Silves station (one of the cheapest rail journeys in Portugal, ~€1.50). Explore the magnificent Moorish Silves Castle (€3 entry) with panoramic views over the orange groves.
day_by_day.afternoon: Wander through Silves old town, visit the Gothic Sé Catedral de Silves (free or small donation), and browse the riverside market stalls. Walk along the banks of the Arade River.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Silves before catching the evening train back to Lagoa. Silves has excellent budget restaurants serving traditional Algarvian cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Padaria (bakery) near Lagoa station — fresh bread roll and coffee (~€2)
meals.lunch: Café Restaurante O Castelo in Silves — grilled chicken piri-piri or cataplana stew (~€9-11)
meals.dinner: Restaurante Marisqueira Rui in Silves — famous for grilled fish; ask for the prato do dia (dish of the day) (~€10-12)

day_by_day.notes: Train from Lagoa to Silves takes about 10 minutes. Silves is a UNESCO-listed heritage site and one of the most historically rich towns in the Algarve. Wear comfortable walking shoes for the castle cobblestones.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Praia da Marinha — considered one of the most beautiful beaches in Europe and accessible from Lagoa (~15 min by taxi or bike rental). Arrive early to explore the sea caves and grottos accessible at low tide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk the coastal cliff trail from Praia da Marinha toward Benagil — a stunning 3km coastal path with incredible sea views (free). Stop to admire Praia do Paraíso and other hidden coves along the way.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagoa and enjoy a wine tasting evening at a local wine bar. Try Lagoa's regional wines including the white Arinto and red Negra Mole varieties.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or local café — yogurt, fruit, and coffee (~€3-4)
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic from the local supermarket (Pingo Doce or Lidl in Lagoa) — bread, local cheese, olives, and fruit (~€4-5)
meals.dinner: Restaurante A Lagosteira in Lagoa — local seafood with house wine (~€12-14 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Praia da Marinha has very limited parking and gets crowded in peak season. September is ideal as crowds thin out. The cliff walk to Benagil is moderate difficulty — bring water. Low tide is best for cave exploration.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the famous Benagil Sea Cave — take a kayak or stand-up paddleboard rental from Praia de Benagil (~€15-20 for 2 hours) to paddle into the iconic domed cave. Book early as it gets busy.
day_by_day.afternoon: Relax on Praia de Benagil beach, one of the smallest and most charming beaches in the Algarve, nestled between golden cliffs. Swim and sunbathe in the sheltered cove.
day_by_day.evening: Head back to Lagoa for a quiet evening. Visit the Largo da Igreja square for a sundowner drink at a terrace café while watching local life unfold.

meals.breakfast: Café in Lagoa — coffee and pastel de nata (~€2)
meals.lunch: Snack bar at Benagil beach — fresh fish sandwich or bifana (pork sandwich) (~€6-8)
meals.dinner: Churrasqueira (grill house) in Lagoa — half chicken piri-piri with fries and salad (~€8-10)

day_by_day.notes: Benagil Cave can also be seen from the cliff top for free if you prefer not to rent a kayak. Budget boat tours from Benagil beach to the cave run ~€10 per person. September water temperature is around 22°C — perfect for swimming.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip west to Portimão — take the bus from Lagoa (~€2, 20 min). Visit the Museu de Portimão (€3 entry), an award-winning museum housed in a former fish canning factory, exploring Algarve's fishing heritage.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk across the bridge to Ferragudo, a charming whitewashed fishing village with a medieval castle (exterior free) and a beautiful beach, Praia Grande de Ferragudo. Swim and relax.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Ferragudo village — it has some excellent seafood restaurants at reasonable prices compared to touristy Portimão. Watch the sunset over the Arade River estuary.

meals.breakfast: Café in Lagoa before departure (~€2.50)
meals.lunch: Tasca in Ferragudo — grilled sea bream (dourada) with vegetables and local wine (~€11-13)
meals.dinner: Restaurante O Sueste in Ferragudo — seafood rice or grilled fish with a carafe of house wine (~€12-14 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Ferragudo is one of the most authentic and least touristy villages in the Algarve. The ferry between Portimão and Ferragudo costs about €1. Bus back to Lagoa runs until late evening.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and leisure morning — sleep in, enjoy a slow breakfast, and explore Lagoa's local market if it falls on a market day (check locally). Browse fresh produce, local honey, almonds, and Algarve handicrafts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Adega Cooperativa do Lagoa or another local winery for an affordable wine tour and tasting (~€5-10). Lagoa is the heart of Algarve wine production — taste the distinctive local whites, reds, and medronho (arbutus brandy).
day_by_day.evening: Self-catered evening using local market finds — set up a picnic-style dinner in your accommodation or in a local park with local wine, cheese, cured meats, and bread.

meals.breakfast: Extended breakfast at a local café — eggs, toast, juice, and coffee (~€5-6)
meals.lunch: Market snacks — local olives, bread, and regional cheese (~€4-5)
meals.dinner: Self-catered picnic with market produce and a bottle of local Lagoa wine (~€8-10 total)

day_by_day.notes: Mid-trip rest day is important for recharging. Lagoa's wine cooperative is one of the best-value wine experiences in the Algarve. Local medronho (firewater) is a traditional digestif worth trying — very affordable at local shops.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip east to Albufeira — take the bus (~€3, 30 min). Walk through the old town (Albufeira Velha), visit the Igreja de Sant'Ana, and browse the colourful fishing boats on the beach below the cliff.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Praia dos Pescadores (Fishermen's Beach) in Albufeira — a lively beach in the heart of the old town. Explore the sea tunnel carved through the cliff connecting the beach to the old town square.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Albufeira's Rua Cândido dos Reis (the famous strip) for a lively evening atmosphere. Have dinner at a local restaurant away from the main tourist drag for better prices.

meals.breakfast: Café in Lagoa before bus departure (~€2.50)
meals.lunch: Restaurante O Penedo in Albufeira old town — grilled fish prato do dia (~€9-11)
meals.dinner: Tasca near Albufeira old town market — traditional cataplana or açorda de mariscos (seafood bread stew) (~€11-13)

day_by_day.notes: Albufeira can be very touristy but the old town retains authentic charm. Avoid the strip restaurants which are overpriced — walk 5 minutes inland for much better value. Last bus back to Lagoa departs around 22:00.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Praia da Galé — a long, wide sandy beach between Lagoa and Albufeira, easily reached by bus or a 30-minute bike ride. One of the quieter beaches in the area with beautiful dune scenery.
day_by_day.afternoon: Coastal walk from Praia da Galé toward Praia da Salgados — a nature reserve beach with a freshwater lagoon behind it, home to flamingos and migratory birds. Excellent free birdwatching.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagoa for a relaxed evening. Visit a local wine shop to pick up a bottle of Algarve wine for under €5 and enjoy it on the hotel terrace or balcony.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or local padaria — fresh bread with local fig jam and coffee (~€3)
meals.lunch: Beach snack bar at Galé — grilled sardines with bread and a cold beer (~€8-9)
meals.dinner: Restaurante Barão in Lagoa — bacalhau (salt cod) dish of the day with potatoes and salad (~€10-12)

day_by_day.notes: Praia da Salgados is a protected nature area — no beach facilities but spectacular natural scenery. Bring binoculars if you have them for birdwatching. September is excellent for migratory bird sightings.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Lagos — take the train from Lagoa station (~€3.50, 40 min). Explore Lagos old town, the historic slave market (Mercado de Escravos, €3 entry), and the impressive town walls.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to Ponta da Piedade — a dramatic headland with extraordinary rock formations, sea arches, and emerald green waters (free entry). One of the most photographed spots in the Algarve. Hire a kayak (~€15) to explore the sea caves up close.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Lagos before catching the train back. Lagos has excellent budget dining options in the old town.

meals.breakfast: Café near Lagoa station (~€2.50)
meals.lunch: Mercado de Lagos food hall — fresh seafood, local cheese, and produce (~€8-10)
meals.dinner: Restaurante Adega in Lagos old town — grilled tuna steak with potatoes and salad, house wine (~€12-14)

day_by_day.notes: Lagos is one of the most beautiful towns in the Algarve and well worth the day trip. The train journey is scenic and affordable. Last train back to Lagoa is around 22:30. Ponta da Piedade is a 2km walk from Lagos town centre.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the inland Algarve — rent a bicycle or take a local bus toward Estombar village (5 min from Lagoa). Walk along the Arade River trail through orange and carob groves — a peaceful, free nature walk.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Caldas de Monchique in the hills above Portimão — a historic spa village with thermal springs (bus from Portimão ~€3). Walk through the eucalyptus forest and visit the free public fountain with mineral water.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagoa via Portimão. Stop for a final wine tasting at a local Lagoa wine bar — try to find a bar offering Algarve wine flights for a comparative tasting experience.

meals.breakfast: Local padaria in Lagoa — croissant and coffee (~€2)
meals.lunch: Café in Caldas de Monchique — local presunto (cured ham) sandwich and regional honey cake (~€6-7)
meals.dinner: Lagoa town centre restaurant — espetada (meat skewer) with salad and local wine (~€11-13)

day_by_day.notes: Caldas de Monchique is a hidden gem rarely visited by tourists. The thermal spa hotel offers day access to pools for around €15 if you want a treat. The inland Algarve has a completely different landscape from the coast — lush and forested.

day_by_day.morning: Final beach day — return to your favourite beach from the trip (Praia da Marinha or Carvoeiro recommended). Take a final morning swim, collect some smooth pebbles as free souvenirs, and enjoy the Algarve sunshine.
day_by_day.afternoon: Souvenir shopping in Lagoa town — visit local ceramic shops for hand-painted azulejo tiles, pick up local wine, almond sweets (Dom Rodrigo), fig cake (morgado), and dried figs to take home. All affordable and authentically Algarvian.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner — splurge slightly on a nicer restaurant for a celebratory last dinner. Try a traditional cataplana (Algarve's iconic copper pot seafood stew) as a final memorable meal.

meals.breakfast: Slow café breakfast in Lagoa — full Portuguese breakfast with eggs, toast, juice, and coffee (~€6-7)
meals.lunch: Beach snack bar — final grilled sardines with crusty bread and cold Sagres beer (~€8-9)
meals.dinner: Restaurante Vila Lisa in Lagoa or nearby — cataplana de marisco (seafood cataplana) with local white wine (~€18-22 per person, a worthy splurge)

day_by_day.notes: Dom Rodrigo almond sweets and fig cake are the most iconic Algarve food souvenirs and available cheaply at local supermarkets and delis. A bottle of local Lagoa wine makes an excellent budget gift (~€4-7). Pack purchases carefully to avoid breakage.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Lagoa — pack bags, check out of the hotel, and enjoy a last slow coffee and pastel de nata at a local café. Take a final stroll through Lagoa town to say goodbye.
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer to Faro Airport — take the Eva Bus from Lagoa to Faro (~€5, allow 1.5 hours including connection). Arrive at the airport with plenty of time for departure.
day_by_day.evening: Departure — reflect on 13 wonderful days in the Algarve. No activities scheduled.

meals.breakfast: Final café stop in Lagoa — coffee and pastel de nata (~€2)
meals.lunch: Airport café or grab a final bifana (pork sandwich) from a café near the bus station before departure (~€4-5)
meals.dinner: On flight or at destination

day_by_day.notes: Check bus times the night before to ensure you catch the right connection to Faro Airport. Allow extra time as September can see heavier tourist traffic. Keep some euros for airport coffee or last-minute purchases. Total estimated budget for 13 days excluding flights and accommodation: approximately €350-450 per person covering transport, meals, activities, and souvenirs.

trip_options.title: Classic Portugal Algarve Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Faro Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer from Faro Airport to Lagoa Boutique Stay (approx. 40 min drive). Check in, freshen up, and take a leisurely stroll through the charming town of Lagoa, exploring the central square, the Igreja Matriz de Lagoa church, and local shops to get your bearings
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a relaxed welcome dinner in Lagoa town center, sampling traditional Algarvian cuisine including fresh grilled fish or cataplana seafood stew

meals.breakfast: On the flight or grab a snack at Faro Airport
meals.lunch: Light snack or café meal near the hotel after check-in
meals.dinner: Restaurante O Leão in Lagoa — traditional Portuguese cuisine, mid-range pricing, great local atmosphere

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light to recover from travel. Pick up a local SIM card or confirm roaming at the airport. Ask hotel staff for restaurant recommendations and local tips.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Praia de Carvoeiro, one of the most picturesque beaches in the Algarve, just 5 km from Lagoa. Explore the dramatic golden cliffs, swim in the clear Atlantic waters, and walk the scenic coastal boardwalk
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the stunning Algar Seco rock formations — a short walk east of Carvoeiro beach. Marvel at the natural arches, caves, and sea grottos carved into the limestone cliffs. Great for photos and light hiking
day_by_day.evening: Return to Carvoeiro village for dinner in one of the seafront restaurants overlooking the beach

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a local pastelaria in Lagoa for pastéis de nata and coffee
meals.lunch: Picnic on the beach with local bread, cheese, and fruit from a Lagoa supermarket, or a casual café in Carvoeiro
meals.dinner: Restaurante O Castelo in Carvoeiro — fresh seafood with ocean views, mid-range prices

day_by_day.notes: Carvoeiro is only 5 km from Lagoa — easy by taxi, rideshare, or rental car. Wear comfortable walking shoes for Algar Seco. September weather is typically warm and sunny — ideal beach conditions.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Adega do Cantor winery near Guia (approx. 15 km from Lagoa), famously co-owned by Sir Cliff Richard. Take a guided tour of the estate, learn about Algarvian wine production, and enjoy a tasting of their award-winning Vida Nova and Onda Nova wines
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Praia da Galé, a long golden sandy beach near Albufeira (approx. 20 km from Lagoa). Relax on the beach, swim, and enjoy the more laid-back atmosphere compared to busier Albufeira beaches
day_by_day.evening: Explore the old town of Albufeira for dinner — wander the cobblestone streets, browse local shops, and dine in the historic quarter

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Beach snack bar at Praia da Galé or bring a picnic
meals.dinner: A Ruína restaurant in Albufeira old town — iconic seafood restaurant built into cliff ruins, moderate pricing

day_by_day.notes: Book the Adega do Cantor winery tour in advance as spots fill quickly. Wine tasting typically costs €10–€20 per person. A rental car makes this day much easier.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Silves, the ancient Moorish capital of the Algarve (approx. 12 km from Lagoa). Explore the magnificent red sandstone Castelo de Silves, one of the best-preserved Moorish castles in Portugal, with panoramic views over the surrounding countryside
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Silves town further — visit the Gothic Sé Cathedral, browse the local market, and walk along the Arade River. Stop at a local cork workshop to see traditional cork products being made
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Silves — the town has excellent traditional restaurants known for hearty Algarvian inland cuisine

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Café Inglês in Silves, located within the castle walls — charming atmosphere, light meals and local dishes
meals.dinner: Restaurante Marisqueira Rui in Silves — famous for grilled fish and shellfish, very popular with locals, mid-range prices

day_by_day.notes: Castle entrance fee is approximately €3–€5. Silves is a great contrast to the coastal towns — more authentic and less touristy. The town is very walkable.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to Portimão (approx. 10 km from Lagoa) and visit Praia da Rocha, one of the Algarve's most famous beaches. Enjoy the wide expanse of golden sand backed by dramatic ochre cliffs and explore the sea caves accessible by foot at low tide
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Portimão Museum (Museu de Portimão), housed in a beautifully restored 19th-century sardine canning factory. Fascinating exhibits on local fishing heritage, archaeology, and Algarvian history — entry is free or low cost
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the Portimão marina waterfront, browse the restaurants and bars, and enjoy the lively atmosphere

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Fresh sardines at a beachside restaurant at Praia da Rocha — Portimão is famous for its grilled sardines
meals.dinner: Taberna da Maré near Portimão marina — excellent grilled fish and local wines, mid-range pricing

day_by_day.notes: Museum is closed on Mondays. Portimão is very easy to reach from Lagoa by bus or car. The marina area is great for an evening walk.

day_by_day.morning: Take a boat trip from Portimão or Carvoeiro to explore the spectacular sea caves, grottos, and golden rock formations of the Algarve coastline. Many tours include stops at hidden beaches accessible only by boat
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Praia do Carvalho, a secluded hidden beach near Carvoeiro accessed through a tunnel carved through the cliffs. Enjoy swimming and sunbathing in this magical, less-crowded spot
day_by_day.evening: Wine tasting evening — visit a local wine bar in Lagoa or Carvoeiro focusing on Alentejo and Algarve regional wines, including Loureiro, Arinto, and Negra Mole varieties

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic for the boat trip or eat at a café in Carvoeiro after
meals.dinner: Restaurante O Barradas near Silves — family-run restaurant with excellent regional cuisine and local wine selection, mid-range

day_by_day.notes: Book the boat trip in advance — tours depart from Portimão or Carvoeiro and typically cost €15–€30 per person. Praia do Carvalho requires a short cliff walk — wear appropriate footwear.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Lagos (approx. 25 km west of Lagoa). Start with a visit to the famous Ponta da Piedade, a breathtaking headland with extraordinary rock formations, sea arches, and emerald-green waters — one of the Algarve's most iconic sights
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Lagos old town — walk the historic city walls, visit the Igreja de Santo António with its stunning baroque interior, and browse the Mercado de Lagos. Relax at Meia Praia, a long sandy beach just outside the town
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy dinner and the vibrant nightlife of Lagos — the town has a great mix of traditional restaurants and lively bars

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Casinha do Petisco in Lagos — charming local tasca with excellent petiscos (Portuguese tapas) and fresh fish
meals.dinner: Restaurante Dom Sebastião in Lagos old town — classic Portuguese cuisine in a historic setting, mid-range prices

day_by_day.notes: Lagos is easily reachable by train from Portimão or by car. Ponta da Piedade is best visited in the morning before crowds arrive. Consider a kayak tour of the rock formations for an unforgettable experience.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Quinta dos Vales estate near Estômbar (approx. 8 km from Lagoa) — a beautiful wine estate and sculpture park. Take a guided tour of the vineyards and wine cellar, followed by a tasting of their acclaimed Algarve wines
day_by_day.afternoon: Relax at Praia de Benagil, one of the Algarve's most photographed beaches, famous for the spectacular Benagil Sea Cave (Algar de Benagil). Take a kayak, paddleboard, or small boat tour to enter the cave
day_by_day.evening: Sunset drinks at a clifftop bar near Lagoa or Carvoeiro, watching the Atlantic sunset over the golden cliffs

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the Quinta dos Vales estate café or a nearby restaurant in Estômbar
meals.dinner: Restaurante Rei das Praias in Armação de Pêra — excellent fresh seafood, popular with locals, mid-range

day_by_day.notes: Quinta dos Vales tours should be booked in advance (approximately €15–€25 per person including tasting). The Benagil Cave is extremely popular — arrive early or book a guided boat tour in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Armação de Pêra beach (approx. 8 km from Lagoa), one of the longest beaches in the Algarve. Enjoy a morning swim and walk along the promenade. Visit the small 17th-century chapel of Santo António perched on the cliff edge
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a guided jeep safari or off-road tour into the Algarve hinterland — explore traditional villages, ancient windmills, orange and almond orchards, and the authentic rural Algarve away from the coast
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagoa for a relaxed dinner and evening stroll through the town

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Traditional village restaurant during the jeep safari tour — typically included or available as an add-on
meals.dinner: Adega Canastro in Lagoa — traditional wine cellar restaurant with local Algarvian dishes and excellent house wine, mid-range

day_by_day.notes: Jeep safaris typically cost €35–€55 per person and depart from various points in the Algarve. Book through local tour operators. A great way to see the non-beach side of the Algarve.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to Sagres and Cabo de São Vicente (approx. 60 km from Lagoa) — the southwesternmost point of mainland Europe. Visit the dramatic Fortaleza de Sagres and stand at the windswept cliffs of Cabo de São Vicente lighthouse, a truly awe-inspiring location
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Sagres town and visit Praia do Martinhal or Praia de Sagres — beautiful, wilder Atlantic beaches with excellent conditions for surfing. Even non-surfers can enjoy watching the waves and the rugged scenery
day_by_day.evening: Drive back toward Lagos or Portimão for dinner before returning to Lagoa

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Restaurante A Tasca in Sagres — excellent fresh fish, very popular with locals, good value
meals.dinner: Restaurante Adega Vilalisa in Mexilhoeira Grande (on the way back) — renowned for traditional Algarvian cuisine, mid-range

day_by_day.notes: This is a longer driving day — approximately 1.5 hours each way. Start early to make the most of the day. The sunset at Cabo de São Vicente is legendary but the drive back in the dark requires care. Consider staying for sunset then driving back.

day_by_day.morning: Relaxed morning — enjoy the hotel amenities, have a long breakfast, and explore any remaining corners of Lagoa town. Visit the local market if it's running (check days with hotel) for local produce, honey, almonds, and artisan goods
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Praia de Marinha (approx. 10 km from Lagoa), consistently rated one of the most beautiful beaches in Europe. Walk the clifftop coastal trail from Benagil to Marinha for spectacular views, then descend to the beach for a swim
day_by_day.evening: Special wine dinner — book a wine pairing dinner at a local restaurant in the Lagoa area, sampling the best of Algarve and Alentejo wines paired with regional dishes

meals.breakfast: Leisurely hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Snack bar at Praia de Marinha or bring a picnic
meals.dinner: Restaurante Vila Lisa in Mexilhoeira Grande — celebrated restaurant known for exceptional traditional Algarvian cuisine and extensive wine list, slightly splurge-worthy for a special evening

day_by_day.notes: Praia de Marinha is one of the most photographed beaches in Portugal — arrive before midday even in September to secure a good spot. The coastal walk is approximately 5 km one way.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Arade River estuary nature reserve near Portimão for a peaceful morning birdwatching and nature walk — a great contrast to the busy beaches. September is an excellent month for migratory birds
day_by_day.afternoon: Final beach afternoon — revisit your favorite beach from the trip or try Praia dos Três Castelos near Portimão, a quieter beach with beautiful rock formations. Enjoy a last long swim in the Atlantic
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner — celebrate the trip with a special meal in Portimão or Carvoeiro, choosing the best restaurant you've discovered during your stay

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Beachside snack bar or café
meals.dinner: Buzio Restaurante in Portimão — excellent seafood and Portuguese cuisine, great atmosphere for a farewell dinner, mid-range to slightly above

day_by_day.notes: Use this day to do any last-minute souvenir shopping — look for local products like Algarvian honey, medronho (local firewater), dried figs, almond sweets, and local wine to take home.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in the Algarve — enjoy a leisurely last hotel breakfast. Take a short walk around Lagoa one final time to soak in the atmosphere. Visit a local pastelaria for a last pastel de nata and espresso
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of the hotel and transfer to Faro Airport (approx. 40 min drive). Allow plenty of time for check-in and security. Browse the airport shops for any last-minute Portuguese gifts including wine, port, and pastries
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Faro Airport

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast — enjoy it slowly
meals.lunch: Light meal at Faro Airport or a café in Lagoa before departure
meals.dinner: Airport restaurant or on the flight

day_by_day.notes: Check hotel checkout time in advance (usually 11:00–12:00). Faro Airport has reasonable dining and shopping options. Allow at least 2 hours before departure for check-in. Consider booking a taxi or transfer in advance for a stress-free journey to the airport.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Portugal Algarve Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Praia da Marinha Coastal Walk and Swim
experiences.description: Explore the dramatic golden limestone cliffs and crystal-clear coves of Praia da Marinha, consistently rated one of Europe's most beautiful beaches. The coastal walking trail connecting Marinha to Benagil takes roughly 90 minutes and rewards hikers with stunning sea views and hidden grottos. Staying in Carvoeiro or Lagoa places you within a 10-minute drive, making this a seamless half-day activity without long transfers.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival — Flight LH lands at 13:00. No morning activities scheduled. Private transfer from Faro Airport to Lagoa Boutique Stay arranged in advance.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to Lagoa Boutique Stay and settle into your luxury suite. Freshen up and take a leisurely orientation stroll through the charming village of Lagoa, exploring the local square and admiring the traditional whitewashed architecture.
day_by_day.evening: Welcome dinner at a top-rated Lagoa restaurant. Enjoy a curated tasting menu featuring fresh Algarve seafood — grilled tiger prawns, percebes, and locally caught sea bass — paired with a premium Alentejo white wine.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable (in-flight)
meals.lunch: Light bite at the airport or en route — artisan sandwich and fresh juice at a premium airport lounge
meals.dinner: Fine dining at Restaurante O Barradas (Silves/Lagoa area) — tasting menu with local seafood and Algarve wine pairings

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private airport transfer in advance. Request early check-in if possible. Keep Day 1 relaxed to recover from travel.

day_by_day.morning: Praia da Marinha Coastal Walk and Swim — Explore the dramatic golden limestone cliffs and crystal-clear coves of one of Europe's most celebrated beaches. Take the scenic clifftop trail and descend to the secluded beach for a morning swim in turquoise waters.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private boat tour departing from Benagil — cruise along the stunning sea caves, arches, and grottos of the Algarve coastline, including the iconic Benagil Cave. Enjoy chilled Champagne and fresh fruit on board.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at a clifftop bar near Carvoeiro, followed by dinner at a premium restaurant specializing in cataplana — the traditional Algarvian copper-pot seafood stew.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at the hotel — fresh pastries, local cheeses, smoked fish, and tropical fruit
meals.lunch: Picnic-style gourmet hamper on the boat tour — charcuterie, local cheeses, crusty bread, and chilled rosé
meals.dinner: Restaurante Bon Bon (Carvoeiro) — Michelin-starred dining with creative Algarvian cuisine

day_by_day.notes: Book the private boat tour at least 2 days in advance. Bring reef-safe sunscreen, snorkeling gear, and a beach towel. Praia da Marinha access involves a short cliff descent.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Quinta dos Vales winery near Estômbar (15 minutes from Lagoa) — a premium Algarve estate known for award-winning reds and whites. Enjoy a guided vineyard tour, learn about the terroir and winemaking process, and explore the sculpture garden.
day_by_day.afternoon: Exclusive wine tasting session at Quinta dos Vales — sample 6–8 reserve and premium wines paired with local charcuterie, artisan cheeses, and Algarve honey. Option to purchase bottles for the trip.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening in Lagoa — visit the historic Igreja Matriz de Lagoa and browse the local artisan shops. Dinner at a curated wine-focused restaurant in Lagoa village.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — eggs Benedict, fresh juices, local honey, and artisan bread
meals.lunch: Wine and food pairing at the winery — charcuterie boards, local cheeses, olives, and reserve wines
meals.dinner: Adega do Cantor (Guia, 20 min) — celebrity-owned estate restaurant with exceptional Portuguese cuisine and wine list

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book the winery tour and tasting experience. Quinta dos Vales offers private VIP tastings with the winemaker — highly recommended for a luxury upgrade.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Praia de Benagil — arrive early to beat the crowds and enjoy the pristine sands. Take a guided kayak or paddleboard session along the coast, exploring hidden sea arches and caves accessible only by water.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Armação de Pêra — relax on one of the Algarve's longest and most beautiful beaches. Rent a private beach cabana with butler service for the afternoon. Optional jet ski or parasailing experience.
day_by_day.evening: Drive to Portimão for dinner at a premium riverside restaurant. Enjoy fresh grilled fish, Algarvian cataplana, and local Vinho Verde overlooking the Arade River.

meals.breakfast: Continental breakfast at the hotel with fresh pastries and seasonal fruit
meals.lunch: Beachside seafood at a premium chiringuito (beach restaurant) near Benagil — grilled octopus, gambas al ajillo, and chilled white wine
meals.dinner: Restaurante Titanic (Portimão) — upscale riverside dining with outstanding fresh fish and shellfish

day_by_day.notes: Arrive at Benagil before 9:00 AM for the best experience. Private beach cabana at Armação de Pêra can be arranged through the hotel concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Silves — the ancient Moorish capital of the Algarve. Explore the magnificent red sandstone Silves Castle (Castelo de Silves) with panoramic views over orange groves and the Arade River valley.
day_by_day.afternoon: Wine tasting at Quinta do Francês — a boutique organic winery in the Silves hills producing exceptional single-varietal wines from indigenous Portuguese grapes. Private tour and barrel-room tasting with the owner.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Silves old town — dine al fresco at a premium restaurant on the cobbled streets below the castle, enjoying slow-roasted lamb, migas, and a bottle of premium Algarve red.

meals.breakfast: Full gourmet hotel breakfast — smoked salmon, avocado, poached eggs, and fresh-squeezed orange juice
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a riverside café in Silves — fresh bread, local olives, sheep's cheese, and cold cuts
meals.dinner: Restaurante Marisqueira Rui (Silves) — legendary seafood restaurant famous for its shellfish platters and cataplana

day_by_day.notes: Silves is only 10 km from Lagoa — an easy drive or taxi ride. The castle entrance fee is minimal. Quinta do Francês requires advance booking for private tours.

day_by_day.morning: Luxury spa morning at the hotel or a nearby 5-star spa resort (e.g., Vila Vita Parc in Porches, 10 minutes away). Enjoy a 90-minute couples' massage, hydrotherapy pool, and steam room.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private wine and gastronomy tour of the Lagoa wine region — the Algarve's most celebrated wine appellation. Visit two boutique quintas producing the region's signature Negra Mole and Crato Branco varietals.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset dinner at Vila Vita Parc's Ocean restaurant — one of Portugal's most celebrated fine dining experiences with two Michelin stars. Book well in advance.

meals.breakfast: Light spa-friendly breakfast — Greek yogurt, granola, fresh berries, and herbal teas
meals.lunch: Wine and tapas pairing at the second winery visited — fresh bread, local cheeses, fig jam, and premium reserve wines
meals.dinner: Ocean Restaurant at Vila Vita Parc — 2 Michelin-star tasting menu with wine pairing (approx. €200–€300 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Ocean Restaurant at Vila Vita Parc requires reservations weeks in advance. Smart dress code enforced. This is the culinary highlight of the trip — an unmissable luxury experience.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Sagres and Cape St. Vincent — the southwestern tip of continental Europe. Walk the dramatic clifftops, visit the historic Sagres Fortress, and watch the Atlantic waves crash against the ancient lighthouse.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the wild and untouched beaches of Costa Vicentina — Praia do Beliche and Praia do Tonel offer dramatic scenery and excellent surf. Enjoy a swim or simply relax on the remote sands.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back east toward Lagos for dinner — one of the Algarve's most vibrant and beautiful towns. Stroll the historic old town and dine at a premium restaurant in the marina district.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — full gourmet spread with local pastries and fresh juices
meals.lunch: Seafood lunch at a clifftop restaurant in Sagres — grilled barnacles, fresh tuna steak, and local wine
meals.dinner: No Pátio (Lagos) — intimate fine dining with creative modern Portuguese cuisine and excellent wine cellar

day_by_day.notes: Sagres is approximately 70 km from Lagoa — allow 1 hour each way. The drive along the EN125 and EN268 is scenic. Bring a light jacket as the Atlantic wind at Cape St. Vincent can be strong even in September.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Lagos old town on foot — visit the Ponta da Piedade rock formations at sunrise for golden-hour photography. Descend via wooden walkways to sea-level viewpoints for breathtaking views of the ochre sea stacks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private yacht charter from Lagos Marina — sail along the golden coastline, anchor at secluded coves for swimming and snorkeling, and enjoy a catered lunch on deck with chilled wines.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagoa for a relaxed evening. Visit a local tasca (traditional tavern) for a casual but premium experience — petiscos (Portuguese tapas), local craft beer, and medronho (arbutus berry spirit).

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at a Lagos café — pastel de nata, fresh coffee, and local bread with butter and honey
meals.lunch: Catered gourmet lunch on the private yacht — fresh seafood, charcuterie, artisan cheeses, and premium rosé
meals.dinner: Tasca do Celso (Lagoa area) — intimate local restaurant with outstanding petiscos and regional specialties

day_by_day.notes: Ponta da Piedade is best visited at golden hour — plan to arrive by 7:30–8:00 AM. Private yacht charter from Lagos Marina can be arranged for half-day or full-day. Prices start from approximately €600 for a half-day private charter.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Praia da Rocha (Portimão) — one of the Algarve's most iconic beaches with dramatic red cliffs. Morning swim followed by a beach yoga or meditation session arranged through the hotel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Portimão city exploration — visit the Museu de Portimão (housed in a former sardine canning factory), stroll the riverside promenade, and browse the artisan market for local crafts and ceramics.
day_by_day.evening: Portimão is famous for its grilled sardines — join a premium sardine grilling experience at a traditional riverside restaurant, paired with local wines and traditional side dishes.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — full spread with seasonal fruits, local jams, and freshly baked bread
meals.lunch: Beachside lunch at a premium chiringuito at Praia da Rocha — grilled sea bream, salad, and chilled white wine
meals.dinner: Taberna da Maré (Portimão) — award-winning restaurant specializing in traditional Algarve recipes with a modern twist

day_by_day.notes: September is still warm enough for comfortable beach days. Museu de Portimão is free on the first Sunday of the month. The sardine grilling experience is best enjoyed at a traditional adega (wine cellar restaurant).

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of the Algarve's cork oak forests (montado) near Silves — learn about the traditional cork harvesting process, walk among ancient trees, and gain insight into this UNESCO-recognized agricultural heritage.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Herdade dos Pimenteiros — a premium wine estate near Lagoa offering private tours and tastings of their acclaimed Algarve DOC wines. Enjoy a curated pairing with regional tapas in the estate's wine cellar.
day_by_day.evening: Exclusive private chef dinner at the hotel or a rented villa space — a curated 5-course Algarvian tasting menu prepared by a local Michelin-trained chef, with matched wines from the day's winery visits.

meals.breakfast: Light hotel breakfast — yogurt parfait, fresh fruit, and espresso
meals.lunch: Estate lunch at the winery — charcuterie, local cheeses, homemade bread, and reserve wine tasting
meals.dinner: Private chef experience — 5-course tasting menu: amuse-bouche, seafood starter, fish course, meat course, and traditional Algarve desserts (Dom Rodrigo, figos cheios)

day_by_day.notes: Arrange the private chef experience through the hotel concierge at least 3 days in advance. This is an exceptional way to experience authentic Algarvian cuisine in a private setting.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day excursion to the Ria Formosa Natural Park near Faro — a stunning coastal lagoon system of islands, channels, and salt marshes. Board a private boat to explore the barrier islands and pristine beaches of Ilha Deserta.
day_by_day.afternoon: Ilha Deserta — spend the afternoon on this remote, car-free island with pristine white sands and crystal waters. Have lunch at the island's only restaurant, Estamine, renowned for its exceptional fresh seafood.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Faro's historic old town (Cidade Velha) — walk the medieval walls, visit the Cathedral and Bone Chapel, and enjoy a sunset aperitif at a rooftop bar before returning to Lagoa.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — full gourmet spread
meals.lunch: Estamine Restaurant (Ilha Deserta) — legendary for its fresh seafood, grilled fish, and natural setting; reserve in advance
meals.dinner: Faro city centre — premium seafood dinner at Restaurante Dois Irmãos, one of Faro's oldest and most celebrated restaurants

day_by_day.notes: Faro is approximately 45 km from Lagoa (40-minute drive). Private boat to Ilha Deserta departs from Faro's old town pier. Estamine requires advance reservations, especially in September.

day_by_day.morning: Return to Praia da Marinha for a final morning swim and clifftop walk — revisit this iconic beach with fresh eyes after nearly two weeks in the Algarve. Bring a book and enjoy the golden September light on the limestone cliffs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Luxury shopping and souvenir experience in Lagoa and Carvoeiro — visit premium ceramics studios, local artisan shops, and wine merchants to select high-quality mementos: hand-painted azulejos, premium wines, artisan olive oil, and local honey.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell gala dinner at a top Algarve restaurant — celebrate the final evening with a grand seafood feast: live lobster, king crab, percebes, and a magnum of premium Algarve wine or Champagne.

meals.breakfast: Special farewell breakfast at the hotel — full luxury spread with Champagne mimosas and the finest local produce
meals.lunch: Light picnic lunch at Praia da Marinha — gourmet hamper with artisan bread, cheese, charcuterie, and rosé wine
meals.dinner: Restaurante Bon Bon (Carvoeiro) — return visit to the Michelin-starred restaurant for a grand farewell tasting menu with full wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Use the afternoon to finalize any wine or artisan purchases. Request the hotel to arrange proper packaging for wine bottles for travel. Consider purchasing a case of Quinta dos Vales reserve wine to ship home.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely final morning — sleep in, enjoy a long breakfast at the hotel, and take a final stroll through Lagoa village. Visit the local market if it falls on a market day for last-minute artisan purchases.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of Lagoa Boutique Stay. Private transfer to Faro Airport for departure. Allow at least 2 hours before your flight for airport procedures.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Faro Airport. Carry premium Algarve wines, artisan goods, and memories of an extraordinary 13-day luxury journey through Portugal's golden coast.

meals.breakfast: Final gourmet hotel breakfast — savor every last bite of local pastries, fresh fruit, and strong Portuguese coffee
meals.lunch: Light lunch at Faro Airport premium lounge or a nearby café before departure
meals.dinner: In-flight or at destination

day_by_day.notes: Confirm private transfer to Faro Airport the evening before. Check airline regulations for carrying wine and liquids. Request a late checkout from the hotel if your flight departs in the late afternoon or evening.
